messages:
Priya (Design): Quick sync — final pass on the Autoscale controls UI. Loom posted with flows but key asks here: 1) SLO slider states (off / preset / custom) need clearer affordance, 2) Burst toggle is getting lost in the pool card when card density is high, 3) keyboard focus order for pool picker + burst toggle feels non-linear. @Noah can we keep visuals minimal but keyboard-first?
Noah (Frontend): Happy to. Two quick constraints: (a) moving burst toggle out of the dense card helps visibility but increases vertical footprint, (b) keyboard order is driven by DOM order — we can reorder but need product signoff on visual shift. I can prototype a floating burst affordance.
Ava (A11Y): Keyboard-first is 👍. A couple of a11y nits: color contrast for the burst pill (currently ~3.8:1) — needs 4.5:1 for normal text. Also the SLO slider doesn't announce its mode; suggest `aria-valuetext` like "SLO target: 250ms, custom" and an `aria-pressed` for the preset button.
Sam (PM): Important: defaults must be safe for cost. Default SLO should map to a conservative min/max range that prevents runaway burst. We also need guardrail messaging: show a small inline hint when user sets burst >50% that explains cost/latency tradeoff.
Jae (Eng): On implementation: burst is currently just a UI flag that maps to `burst_quota` in the API. If we introduce a floating affordance, we'll need to reconcile with existing pool-level props and ensure it's scoped to the selected pool. Also, can we treat preset SLOs as named profiles in the backend (`preset_id`) to avoid frequent migrations?
Priya (Design): Good call on named profiles. For the SLO slider states, proposal: 1) off = ghosted thumb + label "Disabled", 2) preset = filled track + chip with preset name, 3) custom = filled track + numeric readout. Visual sketches attached in Loom. Microcopy: replace "Burst" with "Burst capacity" and add a tooltip: "Temporary extra GPUs for spikes (billed while active)". Thoughts?
Noah (Frontend): Copy tweak is fine. For aria, I can add: `role=slider`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` for the readout. Example inline: <div role="slider" aria-valuemin="50" aria-valuemax="300" aria-valuenow="250" aria-valuetext="SLO target 250ms">
Ava (A11Y): That helps. Also add visible focus ring and ensure the burst pill is reachable with a single Tab press from the pool picker. Avoid skip links that reorder visually but not in DOM.
Sam (PM): UX question: if user selects a pool with lower capacity than the SLO requires, do we show an inline escalate button to suggest moving to Dedicated? Prefer: soft nudge + cost compare modal. We should not auto-migrate.
Jae (Eng): Agree soft nudge. We'll hook into cost-estimator API to show estimated monthly delta for the selected SLO/pool combo. Edge-case: when burst_quota > pool_max we should cap and show a warning.
Priya (Design): I'll update the mock: move burst to the right side of the pool row as a compact toggle with a `?` icon for the tooltip, adjust contrast, and add focus order note in the spec. Small copy options for the nudge: "This SLO may need more capacity — view options" vs "SLO exceeds pool capacity — explore upgrade." Which is less alarming?
Sam (PM): Lean toward the first one — less scary.
Noah (Frontend): I'll prototype the floating burst pill and keyboard flow tomorrow. If deploy looks good, can we ship to staging behind feature flag?
deploy-bot: deploy/ui-staging v2.14.7 succeeded — https://staging.redwood.dev/deploys/4271
Priya (Design): Thanks team — I'll push updated frames to FigJam and add a11y checklist items. Ping when the prototype is up and I'll run a quick usability pass. :rocket:
